articles.title: Measles Cases Erupt in US After Over 25 Years Without Continuous Spread
articles.summary: A series of major measles outbreaks has prompted the Pan American Health Organization to reassess the country's elimination status.
articles.content: Measles cases have started appearing in the United States after more than 25 years without continuous domestic spread of the disease. The country was officially declared measles-free in 2000, but occasional outbreaks still occurred due to travelers bringing the virus into the country. These isolated incidents did not lead to ongoing transmission of the disease within the US population. However, a recent series of major measles outbreaks has changed this status, prompting the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) to reassess the country's elimination status. The PAHO, which is the regional office of the World Health Organization for the Americas, has now determined that the US should be considered non-eliminated. This decision comes after a significant increase in measles cases, with nearly 2,300 reported nationwide in 2025 and over 5,412 confirmed so far this year. A leading health expert has warned that the resurgence of measles could be the point of no return, as outbreaks become increasingly difficult to control. The resurgence of measles in the US is a stark reminder that maintaining high vaccination rates is crucial to preventing large outbreaks. For measles, achieving herd immunity requires at least 95% of the population to be immune through either vaccination or past infection, as its virus spreads rapidly and easily from person to person. In recent years, however, national measles vaccination rates have been steadily declining, with only 10 states reporting rates above the critical threshold among kindergarteners for the 2025-2026 school year. Experts point to a combination of factors contributing to this trend, including decreasing funding and personnel for public health initiatives as well as wavering confidence in vaccines and scientific expertise among the general population. The appointment of an individual with a history of questioning vaccine safety and efficacy has likely exacerbated these issues by creating confusion around established vaccine guidance. According to health authorities, a significant number of measles cases in the United States result in death, with approximately 1 to 3 out of every 1,000 cases being fatal. The high number of reported deaths in Pennsylvania is particularly concerning, as it suggests that the state's true case rate may be higher than what has been captured by data. With over 1,500 measles cases recorded in the state, this discrepancy raises questions about the accuracy of the reported numbers. Measles can have severe long-term health consequences for survivors, including brain damage and immune amnesia. In individuals who contract the virus, their immune system's "memory" is essentially wiped clean, leaving them vulnerable to other infections. The recent surge in measles cases in the United States serves as a stark reminder of the importance of vaccination and immunity. articles.title: Nationwide air traffic control outage causes thousands of flight cancellations
articles.summary: The disruption resulted in nearly 7,500 flight cancellations, causing widespread travel chaos as airlines pointed to the uncontrollable nature of the ATC outage.
articles.content: A nationwide air traffic control outage has left thousands of passengers stranded across the US. The disruption resulted in nearly 7,500 flight cancellations, causing widespread travel chaos. Air travelers were left to navigate the crisis on their own as airlines pointed to the uncontrollable nature of the ATC outage. According to the Department of Transportation, disruptions caused by uncontrollable factors do not require airlines to provide freebies such as hotel stays or food vouchers. The situation has been exacerbated by the sheer number of cancellations, making it nearly impossible for passengers to get a seat on a flight this weekend. Travelers are now forced to fend for themselves, seeking out alternative arrangements at their own expense. The Department of Transportation's customer service dashboard provides information on passenger compensation for flights disrupted by controllable factors, such as maintenance or crew scheduling, but it does not apply to the current situation. Airlines may offer goodwill vouchers to help out affected customers, but it's essential to understand that these are not guaranteed. When booking travel arrangements such as hotels or rental cars, passengers may be able to claim eligible expenses from their credit card issuer. Airline passengers have certain rights in the US, as outlined by the Department of Transportation. However, there is no law requiring carriers to compensate for disruptions caused by uncontrollable events like weather or air traffic control delays. If your flight is canceled, you're entitled to a full refund, including any add-ons like baggage fees or seat upgrades. This must be refunded in the original form of payment. Airlines have varying policies in place when it comes to disruptions they can control, such as cancellations or delays. The US Department of Transportation's Airline Customer Service Dashboard provides insight into what the 10 largest US airlines promise their customers in these situations, including options for rebooking flights, meal vouchers, and hotel accommodations. When a flight is delayed or canceled, many airlines allow passengers to adjust their travel plans online through their website or mobile app. This can be a more efficient way to make changes than waiting on the phone or visiting a physical customer service location. Travelers affected by flight cancellations can reach out to their airlines for assistance. The contact numbers for major carriers vary, with some providing phone support and others offering alternative methods like text messaging or online chat. Alaska Airlines can be reached at 1-800-252-7522 or via text message to 82008, while Allegiant customers can call 1-702-505-8888. American Airlines offers a similar option at 1-800-433-7300, and Avelo passengers can contact the airline at 1-346-616-9500. Delta customers have access to support through their phone number, 1-800-221-1212, while those with Frontier can try online chat or email for assistance. JetBlue is available at 1-800-538-2583 and Southwest passengers can call 1-800-435-9792. Several airlines offer meal or hotel vouchers to customers experiencing delays or cancellations that result in a wait of three hours or more, including overnight stays. Carriers offering both are listed on the DoT dashboard as part of their contingency plans. If you're unsure about compensation for flight disruptions not listed on the DoT dashboard, it's always best to ask your airline directly. Airlines may offer goodwill gestures during uncontrollable disruptions like winter storms, so don't hesitate to request assistance with meals or hotel accommodations. Some credit card companies provide travel insurance that can reimburse customers for unexpected expenses such as hotels, food, and transportation when flights are disrupted. Major banks like Chase and American Express offer cards with trip protection, which means cardholders who purchased their flights using these cards may be eligible for reimbursement. If your flight has been canceled due to an FAA ground stop, it's essential to be proactive about finding alternative ways to reach your destination. Consider renting a car or taking public transportation like trains or buses as viable options. Delays and cancellations are unavoidable in such situations, but being flexible can make the experience more bearable. Once you've decided on a course of action, set a time limit for yourself to wait for a resolution. If that deadline passes without any progress, it's time to explore other ways to reach your destination, which may also be covered by travel insurance. articles.title: National Airspace Ground Stop Lifted After Thousands Stranded
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop has been lifted after stranding thousands of travelers and canceling over 6,600 flights.
articles.content: The Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop has been lifted after stranding thousands of travelers and canceling over 6,600 flights. The halt on air travel was implemented due to technical issues affecting the FAA's data systems that communicate with airplanes. Eastern time, the agency cited "extraordinary circumstances" as the reason for grounding all flights across the country. This decision was made in response to reasons related to safety, but it has left many passengers stranded at airports like Chicago's O'Hare International Airport. The airport's flight-information boards were filled with cancellations and delays during the ground stop on Friday afternoon. Now, airlines will face a challenging task of getting their operations back on track, which is expected to take several days. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin assured the public late Friday that there was no danger posed by the airspace closure, stating "all your loved ones are safe." The nation's air-traffic control system has been criticized for its outdated technology by top officials. They attribute Friday's widespread flight disruptions to the age of this system, which they say is in dire need of modernization. Duffy and Mullin have called on Congress to allocate $50 billion for upgrading the system, an increase from the previous request of $30 billion made in September. The proposed investment aims to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future. The new voice communication systems, known as IP switches, are being implemented to modernize the national airspace system, replacing outdated analog voice switches that still dominate much of the infrastructure. Duffy and Mullin emphasized that the fault was not related to artificial intelligence or cybersecurity issues, dismissing speculation about these factors contributing to the crisis. In an effort to understand what went wrong, Duffy stated that they were still "working on the details" of the incident, including its cause and how it could be prevented in the future. However, he was unable to provide a guarantee that such an event would not recur when asked if the public should feel safe while flying in US airspace. The traveling public remained stranded at airports across the country, relying on airport monitors for updates only to see their flights delayed or canceled, with little recourse for expenses incurred due to the disruptions. The travel disruptions caused by the FAA's nationwide ground stop continued to unfold as airports struggled to cope with the sheer volume of delayed and canceled flights. According to data from FlightAware, over 10,000 flights had been affected by the stop, with Chicago O'Hare and Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson being among the hardest hit. The latter airport, which holds the distinction of being the world's busiest, saw an astonishing number of cancellations - over 350 as of a given time. This was mirrored at major airports in New York, Boston, Texas, and Denver, where more than 200 flights were canceled. The scale of these disruptions is staggering, leaving thousands of travelers stranded. The cause of the ground stop has been attributed to communications issues rather than safety concerns, according to Homeland Security officials. This assertion was echoed by Mullin, who downplayed the significance of the stop in relation to passenger safety. Instead, he emphasized that the issue lay with communication systems and their ability to effectively manage flight operations. As a result of these disruptions, many planes were forced to take evasive action, diverting or turning around mid-flight. Notable examples include Delta Air Lines Flight 958, which was traveling from Los Angeles to New York's JFK when it turned back and diverted to Cincinnati, while another Delta flight changed course over the Eastern Seaboard and landed in Baltimore instead of its intended destination. Air traffic control measures were in place to mitigate the effects of a nationwide ground stop, but the consequences are still being felt by thousands of passengers. Pilots have access to digital tools that allow them to communicate with air-traffic control and their airline's dispatch team, receiving crucial information on routing and other matters. These digital tools can be particularly useful during situations like the current one, where flights were delayed or canceled en masse. According to Mark Stephens, a retired Delta Air Lines pilot, pilots have developed systems to navigate these kinds of scenarios safely, maintaining safe distances from other aircraft and landing within their limits. The last time a nationwide ground stop occurred was in January 2023, lasting approximately 90 minutes. This is a relatively short duration compared to the current disruption, which has already caused significant delays and cancellations for thousands of travelers. Airline systems remain overwhelmed despite the FAA lifting its nationwide ground stop, resulting in continued disruptions for thousands of travelers. At airports across the country, passengers are facing prolonged delays due to airline issues, with many reporting difficulties rebooking flights after cancellations. The situation is further complicated by higher-than-normal call volumes, as evidenced by a social media post from a train operator, which highlighted ongoing challenges faced by airlines. articles.title: Bobby Pulido accepts award at Latin Grammys
articles.summary: Bobby Pulido accepted an award for best Tejano album at the Latin Grammys while confirming his retirement from music.
articles.content: Bobby Pulido, a Democrat who recently won a competitive race to flip Texas' Republican-held 15th Congressional district, accepted an award for best Tejano album at the Latin Grammys. Onstage, he wore his signature cowboy hat as he confirmed his retirement from music but expressed gratitude for representing both the politics and music of Texas. The win marked Pulido's third time taking home this award in this category, although it was his first victory since being elected to Congress. His presence at the ceremony was a notable moment amidst several other politically charged references. Pulido told the audience that he felt immense pride in representing the Tejano music and culture of Texas. He underscored the significance of being from the Lone Star State and having the opportunity to bring its politics and music to the forefront. The Latin Grammys have a history of hosting performances that address social issues, including racism in American politics and human rights crises in Mexico. As Pulido accepted his award, it was clear that he has a deep connection to the Tejano culture and is committed to representing it on both the national stage and in Congress. The Latin Grammys ceremony was filled with powerful messages of change and representation, echoing a theme that resonated across music and politics. "We have to represent, Pulido said in his speech, emphasizing the importance of using one's voice for positive impact. The message of empowerment was palpable as artists took to the stage to accept their awards. The ceremony saw Daddy Yankee crowned Person of the Year, an honor he wore with pride draped in a flowing cape bearing the Puerto Rican flag. He used his platform to emphasize the significance of Puerto Rico's presence on the map. Silvana Estrada, a Mexican folk musician who has long advocated against femicide in her home country, underscored the critical role musicians play today. We have a super important job, she said, highlighting the responsibility that comes with using one's voice for social justice. The Latin Grammys have long been a celebration of music and culture from across the region. However, this year's ceremony saw a notable shift towards using the platform to address pressing social issues. Brazilian artist Anitta made headlines when she won the award for best pop contemporary Portuguese album, marking the first time an award in that language was given out during the televised event. Anitta used her moment in the spotlight to call for unity and recognition of Black culture in Brazil, highlighting the importance of representation and inclusivity. Her words were a powerful reminder that music can be a catalyst for change and social justice. By using her platform to speak out against erasure and promote cultural preservation, Anitta set an example for artists everywhere. As the ceremony progressed, it became clear that this year's Latin Grammys were not just about celebrating music, but also about amplifying marginalized voices. Artists like Anitta are paving the way for a new generation of musicians who are using their art to advocate for social justice and human rights. The impact of these performances extends far beyond the stage, with many fans taking to social media to express their support and solidarity with the artists speaking out on behalf of their communities. This shift towards more overtly political music is a welcome development, one that reflects the changing times and the growing demand for representation and inclusivity in all areas of society. The Latin Grammys have become more than just an award ceremony for music enthusiasts, but a platform to showcase the intersection of art and politics. According to Sayre, the event's founder, this convergence is not surprising given its purpose - to recognize the diverse musical landscape of Latin America. As political shifts swept across the Western Hemisphere this year, with right-wing movements in some countries and progressive changes in others, music has followed suit, reflecting the changing times. It doesn't split that cleanly, Sayre noted, highlighting the connection between musical and political evolution. The correlation between artistic expression and societal change is undeniable, with music often serving as a reflection of its cultural context. As Sayre aptly put it, I don't think you can ever look at music, or how we value music, as independent from a political landscape." This understanding underscores the significance of events like the Latin Grammys in today's world. articles.title: Social relationships crucial to scaling agricultural innovations
articles.summary: A recent study has highlighted the importance of social relationships in scaling agricultural innovations, which is a complex challenge that requires both technical solutions and strong social connections among actors involved.
articles.content: A recent study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems has shed light on a crucial aspect of climate-oriented agricultural research: the role of social relationships in scaling innovations. While partnerships and institutional collaboration are often emphasized, their connection to the scaling process remains understudied. This lack of understanding hinders efforts to ensure that agricultural advancements reach more farmers, influence policy, and drive lasting transformations. The scaling of agricultural innovations is a complex challenge that requires technical solutions as well as strong social relationships among actors involved in these processes. Trust, partnerships, and collaboration are essential for expanding the reach of agricultural research and development initiatives. However, the current state of knowledge leaves much to be desired, making it difficult to design effective monitoring and evaluation systems. The study "Social capital and scaling in climate-oriented Agricultural Research for Development" investigates how social relationships contribute to the scaling process. By examining existing literature on the topic, researchers aim to better understand the role of trust, closeness, and support among actors involved in agricultural innovation. This knowledge is crucial for strengthening the design, monitoring, and evaluation of scaling processes. The study's findings highlight the need for a more nuanced understanding of social relationships in climate-oriented agricultural research. By exploring the intersection of technical solutions and social dynamics, researchers can develop more effective strategies for scaling innovations that benefit farmers, policymakers, and communities worldwide. The analysis of 273 results reports has revealed a significant gap between reported outcomes and the documentation of social and institutional conditions that can facilitate scaling. This discrepancy suggests that researchers often overlook the importance of these factors in achieving successful scaling. A team of researchers from the International Center for Tropical Agriculture, the University of Copenhagen, and the Gates Foundation analyzed reports covering 261 projects across 12 CGIAR research programs. The reports were submitted between 2018 and 2021 under the former CGIAR Research Program on Climate Change, Agriculture and Food Security. The study has identified three key scaling pathways: scaling out, which involves expanding innovations to more people and places; scaling up, where policies and institutions are influenced by these innovations; and scaling deep, which transforms relationships, practices, and social norms. While the reports provide examples of these pathways, particularly scaling out and scaling up, they often lack a detailed explanation of how partnerships, trust, and institutional collaboration contribute to these processes. The researchers have found that the scaling deep dimension is notably underdeveloped in the analyzed documents, suggesting that this aspect is frequently overlooked in research. This omission can hinder the development of effective strategies for scaling innovations that benefit farmers, policymakers, and communities worldwide. By examining the intersection of technical solutions and social dynamics, researchers can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that facilitate successful scaling. This knowledge can be used to inform the development of more effective scaling strategies that take into account the complex social relationships involved in achieving these goals. The analysis used a statistical model to identify patterns in the reports, categorizing them into four main areas: agricultural systems, climate change adaptation, climate change mitigation, and enabling environments. This exercise revealed 17 distinct topics within these categories. However, the researchers found that the reports often fail to explicitly connect collaborative relationships with scaling outcomes, leaving this potential connection implicit. By recognizing and documenting such connections, it is possible to enhance learning across projects and develop more effective strategies for scaling innovations. The study's findings highlight a gap in documentation, where social capital plays a significant role in research experiences but its relationship with scaling pathways remains unexplored. This lack of systematic documentation hinders the comparison of experiences and limits institutional learning. Examples from the study illustrate how partnerships based on trust and collaboration can facilitate different scaling pathways, such as the dissemination of drought-tolerant bean varieties to over 10,000 farmers across three countries through sustained relationships among national agricultural research organizations, seed companies, and farmer associations. The study highlights another example where collaboration between researchers and governments led to a significant outcome: incorporating agroclimatic information into nationally determined contributions under the Paris Agreement in several countries. This collaboration is exemplified by the Local Technical Agroclimatic Committees (MTA) in Colombia, which demonstrate how sustained interaction among farmers, extension agents, and local authorities can foster trust and facilitate the use of climate information. These committees illustrate a successful model that strengthens relationships between stakeholders. Governments, development organizations, and research programs can benefit from explicitly integrating social capital into their theories of change, planning, and monitoring strategies for scaling agricultural innovations. This involves identifying key actors and relationships and incorporating indicators such as trust, collaboration, network diversity, and participation. The authors also warn that networks can sometimes generate inequalities or exclude certain actors, emphasizing the need to understand these dynamics to promote responsible and inclusive scaling. Ignoring these issues could lead to unintended consequences. To better grasp the role of social capital in scaling pathways, researchers recommend explicitly recognizing and documenting its impact throughout project design, implementation, and monitoring phases. This could improve understanding of the conditions necessary for successful expansion of agricultural innovations. Researchers have highlighted the importance of social relationships in scaling up agricultural innovations, a crucial aspect that has been largely overlooked in previous studies. The study emphasizes that building strong connections among stakeholders is vital for the successful expansion of new farming techniques and technologies. By fostering trust and cooperation, farmers can share knowledge and best practices, leading to more efficient use of resources and improved crop yields. This could ultimately contribute to sustainable food systems and mitigate the impacts of climate change on agriculture. articles.title: Microsoft outage affects millions worldwide
articles.summary: A widespread Microsoft outage on November 12 left millions of people unable to send emails or access workplace tools like Teams.
articles.content: A widespread Microsoft outage on November 12 left millions of people worldwide unable to send emails, access Outlook, or use workplace tools like Teams. This led to a ripple effect that extended far beyond offices and workplaces. For many employees, the disruption was seen as an unexpected bonus - some even joked about it. "Thank you Microsoft," one user quipped, "Can you do this every Friday?" The impact of the outage, however, went well beyond the corporate world. Police departments struggled to receive online crime reports, while hospitals had to rely on alternative communication methods. In some areas, government services were temporarily suspended due to the disruption. This highlighted the degree to which essential public services have come to depend on a single private company's technology. The Microsoft outage exposed how vulnerable critical systems are when they rely on external providers. A seemingly ordinary email outage can have far-reaching consequences for public safety, healthcare, and justice. The incident served as a stark reminder of the risks associated with over-reliance on digital infrastructure. The disruption was felt across multiple jurisdictions, including California and Florida. In Los Angeles County, the Sheriff's Department reported problems with its email system, while the county district attorney's office also experienced disruptions. Law enforcement agencies in other areas, such as Colorado and St. Lucie County, were also affected by the outage. Email troubles plagued British police forces on Thursday, including Dorset, Cumbria, South Wales, Wiltshire, and Dyfed-Powys, which struggled to receive online crime reports. Some British police officers and staff were unable to access their Outlook accounts, a critical tool for their work. However, emergency phone lines remained operational, allowing the public to reach them in times of need. The disruption caused inconvenience but did not compromise safety. In Maine's judicial system, email submissions after 12:30 p.m. on Thursday may have gone unnoticed by courts. This has significant implications for those seeking protection orders, who must now rely on alternative methods to ensure their requests are received. In New York City, evictions scheduled for November 13 were put on hold due to the Microsoft outage. The city's Department of Investigation consulted with the Civil Court before making this decision, highlighting the far-reaching consequences of the disruption. Legislative work and local governments also suffered from the outage. Congressional staffers on Capitol Hill struggled to access their email and calendars, while cities such as Austin, Texas, Jacksonville, Florida, Richmond, Virginia, and Laurel, Maryland, pointed residents to alternative channels for communication. Asian governments were not immune to Microsoft's system failure. Australia's top spy agency confirmed it had been impacted by the glitch, along with its police force. Singapore's Government Technology Agency reported disruptions to government systems, but emergency services and a key identity verification system remained operational. Japan's Foreign Ministry was unable to send or receive emails due to the outage. In Canada, Unity Health Toronto declared a Code Grey alert after staff encountered difficulties sending and receiving emails. Despite this, patient care continued uninterrupted at its hospitals. The hospital network assured that all facilities stayed open. Britain's National Health Service also struggled with Microsoft's system failure. According to reports, healthcare workers faced issues accessing email, appointment information, and patient data. Some services resorted to backup systems or manual records due to the disruption. Email disruptions caused by the Microsoft outage had significant consequences for travelers in Canada and Britain. VIA Rail advised its passengers to use alternative methods to track their train journeys, such as the train tracker or text alerts, due to potential issues with receiving trip emails. In addition to rail services, airlines also experienced email problems, although flight operations were largely unaffected. IndiGo and Cathay Pacific reported difficulties with sending and receiving emails, but passengers were able to access their ticket information through other means if necessary. The scale of the outage is difficult to determine, given Microsoft's vast user base. The company revealed in January that over 450 million paid Microsoft 365 commercial seats existed, but it remains unclear how many users were impacted by the email disruption. The loss of Outlook functionality had far-reaching implications for individuals and businesses alike. Those who relied on verification codes or password-reset links via email to access other accounts may have found themselves locked out of online banking, payment systems, and more, even if those services themselves were functioning normally. The economic impact of the Microsoft outage is still being assessed, but one thing is clear: the productivity losses are substantial. A recent survey conducted by Public Opinion Strategies for Google found that 84% of government employees in the D.C. area rely on Microsoft products to get their work done. This dependence on a single provider has been a concern for years, with many experts warning about the risks of an IT monoculture. A report co-commissioned by Google and the Computer & Communications Industry Association found that Microsoft holds 85% of the U.S. government's office productivity software market. The appeal of using a single platform is undeniable, organizations can simplify their operations by having one provider for email, calendars, meetings, and document sharing. However, it appears that many governments stick with Microsoft due to inertia rather than innovation. According to Google's survey, 59% of respondents who use Microsoft at work say their employers chose the software because it was the most effective tool for their jobs, while 41% say their employers had always used Microsoft and were reluctant to change. A recent Government Accountability Office report highlights the challenges of diversifying IT systems in federal agencies. The report analyzed 24 government departments, revealing that 11 faced technical difficulties when integrating multiple cloud vendors due to interoperability issues and 10 struggled with resource constraints in building a skilled cloud workforce. Microsoft has acknowledged that a technical glitch arose from an earlier network capacity upgrade, which resurfaced after a subsequent network change. The company stated that the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or AI malfunction and apologized for the disruption it caused. This incident underscores the fragility of critical systems in the US. The absence of malicious intent is notable, as Google's warning about hackers four years ago predicted a different scenario. In reality, a routine network change at Microsoft triggered widespread disruptions, impacting courts, government offices, police departments, and hospitals, forcing them to resort to manual processes. articles.title: Hokkaido University and Kyoto University Researchers Study Electron Behavior in Alpha-Gallium Oxide
articles.summary: Researchers at Hokkaido University and Kyoto University have discovered that the effective mass of electrons in alpha-gallium oxide films is approximately 40% of a free electron's mass.
articles.content: Researchers have made a significant discovery about the behavior of electrons in alpha-gallium oxide, a material crucial for power electronic devices that convert electrical energy into various forms. These devices are essential for electric vehicles, renewable energy systems, and industrial equipment, but they often suffer from inefficiency due to heat loss during the process. The ability to withstand high voltages and efficiently transfer electricity while releasing heat effectively is key to making these devices more reliable. Alpha-gallium oxide has shown promise in this regard, as it can handle strong electric fields. However, scientists have yet to fully comprehend how easily electrons move through it or how effectively it dissipates heat, both critical factors for creating dependable electronic devices. To gain a deeper understanding of these properties, researchers at Hokkaido University and Kyoto University created thin films of alpha-gallium oxide using mist chemical vapor deposition. They introduced small amounts of germanium into the material to facilitate electron movement. The addition of germanium allowed the team to manipulate the concentration of electrons in the material by varying the amount added. This enabled them to study how changes in electron density affected the flow of electricity and heat through the films, providing valuable insights for improving device performance. The researchers took a closer look at the electrical properties of alpha-gallium oxide films by measuring electron concentration and thermopower, which is a measure of the voltage generated per unit temperature difference across a material. These measurements revealed an unexpected trend - the effective mass of electrons in these films was approximately 40% of a free electron's mass. This value is higher than the theoretically predicted value of 25%, suggesting that electrons behave differently than expected within alpha-gallium oxide. The study also examined how efficiently heat travels through these films, determining their thermal conductivity to be around 19 watts per meter-kelvin. Notably, this thermal conductivity remained relatively stable even when germanium concentration was increased. Further analysis of the results indicates that incorporating germanium can facilitate electron movement without significantly impacting heat transfer through the material. This finding offers a valuable insight for future device development. The study's findings suggest that alpha-gallium oxide's electrical properties are influenced by the behavior of its electrons, which deviate from theoretical expectations. This unexpected electron behavior may be responsible for the slower-than-predicted flow of electrical current in alpha-gallium oxide devices, a crucial consideration for their development. The research team's experimental approach and thorough analysis provide valuable insights into the material's properties and potential applications. As a result, this study offers a significant contribution to the field of materials science. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-heavier-electron-behavior-slower-electrical.html

articles.title: Sascha Braunig Exhibits Artwork at Portland Art Museum
articles.summary: The exhibition showcases a diverse range of works by artist Sascha Braunig, including paintings and sculptures that explore societal expectations placed on women.
articles.content: Sascha Braunig's paintings are notorious for provoking strong reactions in viewers, a mix of fascination and unease that can be palpable. Her goal is to create a physical response in those who see her work, she explains. Braunig achieves this by juxtaposing vibrant, almost playful colors with twisted, unsettling forms, faces and bodies often bound by wiry tendrils that seem to writhe like living things. These figures frequently appear to be hiding from view, their features blurred as they recede into the surrounding background. The artist's unique style has been on display for nearly two decades, she splits her time between New York and Maine, where she paints with a distinctive verve. Since earning her MFA from Yale in 2008, Braunig has shown her work at numerous prominent galleries and institutions, including Foxy Production in Manhattan. In addition to solo exhibitions, her paintings have also been featured in group shows like the New Museum Triennial and MoMA PS1. Braunig's art often grapples with the societal expectations placed on women, she seeks to expose the tension inherent in conforming to these norms. She examines how women are perceived and presented in society, highlighting the contradictions and complexities of femininity. Braunig's work often explores the tensions between opposing forces. Her artistic vision is deeply intertwined with societal influences and cultural imagery, as she herself acknowledges. She delves into the complexities of gender performance and bodily control in her art. The Portland Art Museum will be hosting Braunig's most extensive exhibition to date, which promises to showcase a diverse range of works. The show features over 45 pieces, including paintings, sculptures, drawings on paper, and sketchbooks, all of which demonstrate Braunig's unique approach to the arts. This solo exhibition at the Portland Art Museum marks her first institutional show in Maine. Sayantan Mukhopadhyay, a curator at PMA, notes that Braunig stands out in the local art scene for her singular style. Braunig's work defies easy categorization, often blurring the lines between opposing concepts. This is precisely what draws people to her art, according to Mukhopadhyay. Olivia Smith, whose gallery now represents Braunig, highlights the artist's ability to create an abstraction that can be perceived as both delicate and forceful. Braunig's creative process begins with a drawing, which she later transforms into a three-dimensional model through embellishment. This intricate model-making technique allows her to bring her sketches to life in a tangible form. The subsequent step involves illuminating the model and painting what she observes, effectively merging the physical and visual aspects of her art. The use of clay resin, wire, and paper in Braunig's maquette process imbues her works with a tactile quality that is both captivating and thought-provoking. As seen in paintings like Warm Leatherette, this technique allows her to create visually striking pieces that seem to leap off the canvas. The resulting artwork is not only aesthetically pleasing but also invites the viewer to engage with it on a deeper level. Braunig's fascination with femininity as a performance is a recurring theme throughout her work. By setting up a scene, complete with velvet curtains and klieg lights, she effectively stages an idea that challenges traditional notions of identity. This theatrical approach underscores the notion that gender, like art itself, is a deliberate construction. Growing up in British Columbia, Canada, Braunig was encouraged by her parents to explore her creative side. Her father, a dentist, and mother, a nurse, both nurtured their own artistic interests outside of work, creating an environment where creativity thrived at home. Braunig's love for art began early on, with Pee-wee's Playhouse being a particular source of inspiration that rivalled the influence of museums in shaping her artistic vision. Braunig's formative years were shaped by early exposure to art institutions, but it was Cooper Union in New York City that truly caught her attention. The school had a notable history of nurturing artists like Lee Krasner and Wangechi Mutu. Her decision to attend the prestigious institution was likely influenced by its reputation for fostering artistic talent. The allure of New York City was undeniable for Braunig, who found it the perfect environment in which to hone her craft. With its vibrant art scene and endless creative possibilities, the city seemed tailor-made for a budding artist like herself. Her passion for the city was so all-consuming that she jokes about being "totally in love with it - although this ardor may have also had a darker side. After completing her studies at Cooper Union, Braunig went on to Yale before moving to Maine in 2010. The decision to relocate to a less expensive area proved to be a turning point for her artistic development. By escaping the high costs of living in New York City, she was able to focus on building her unique style without the burden of multiple jobs. Braunig's exposure to various art movements has clearly had an impact on her work, with many observers drawing parallels between her style and Surrealism. While acknowledging these influences, Braunig is quick to emphasize that her art is not a dreamlike fantasy but rather a deeply personal expression. Her recent output has taken a more autobiographical turn, reflecting a renewed focus on exploring her own experiences and emotions. As Braunig transitioned out of that challenging period last year, she began creating paintings that were more deeply personal than ever before. Her recent show Cauldron at Magenta Plains was a testament to this shift in focus, with its title referencing the tumultuous and transformative nature of midlife as a messy, stew-like experience. In her painting My Death", Braunig described it as an explicit self-portrait that explores her own reanimation - a process of emerging from the void of creative block into a new state of being. The result is a complex and multifaceted work that is both haunting and beautiful to behold, with elements of life force and rejuvenation. Braunig has employed the recurring motif of tentacles in her work once again, but this time they are depicted as a life-giving force connected to a sleeping Braunig figure. The concept of torsion, a twisting motion around an axis, has been reimagined by Braunig in her latest work, where it takes on a more figurative meaning. A fleshy pink figure stands at attention within a gray box, its tiny torso twisted and contorted as if wrung out to dry. The muscular back of the figure faces away from the viewer, while its knees are bent in a dramatic plié. Tentacles of orange and yellow outline its exaggerated form. The figure's head is abruptly truncated by the ceiling of the box, and its arms stop short at the elbows, as if encountering an invisible barrier. The sense of confinement is palpable, but Braunig leaves room for interpretation: has the figure been trapped, or has it somehow managed to break free from its shadowy encasement? articles.title: US President Donald Trump to Join China and Russia Leaders for Trilateral Meeting in Shenzen
articles.summary: The meeting marks the conclusion of Trump's visit to China where he will engage in talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
articles.content: US President Donald Trump is set to join leaders of China and Russia for an unprecedented meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China's tech hub next week. According to Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, this gathering will mark the conclusion of Trump's visit to China, where he will engage in talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Putin. In a call with reporters on Friday night, Wales highlighted the significance of the trilateral meeting. The expiration of the New START treaty between Russia and the United States in February marked a significant shift in nuclear arms policy, removing long-standing caps on their atomic arsenals for the first time in over five decades. Trump has been pushing for a new agreement that includes China, calling for a "new, improved and modernized" deal. This stance contrasts with Russia's proposal to extend the existing treaty by another year. The US rejection of this offer highlights the complexities surrounding nuclear arms control agreements. The three-way summit involving Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin is taking place at a time when tensions are running high between these major world powers. The meeting comes as the global community grapples with various conflicts, including ongoing warfare in Ukraine and escalating tensions with Iran. China's President Xi Jinping is seen as least certain about the value of the upcoming trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. According to officials, Beijing views the meeting as an opportunity for China to demonstrate its growing influence and prestige. By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that it offers a chance to showcase China's rising global status. The trilateral meeting is seen as a coveted chance for Russia to posture itself as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing. The situation with Nvidia, an American technology company, is not expected to be raised by Trump during the meeting. Officials said they don't think Trump will bring up the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang of Nvidia, and was accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The trilateral meeting could overshadow the APEC summit, which brings together 21 economies in Shenzhen to mark a significant moment for China's fast-growing coastal metropolis that has transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub over just a few decades. The trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin could potentially undermine China's efforts to project itself as a champion of free trade at APEC, according to Hoo Tiang Boon, an expert on Chinese foreign policy. China's stance on multilateralism is being put into question by the unprecedented gathering of the three leaders, who have met individually with each other numerous times in the past. "You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism," he said, highlighting the paradoxical nature of this development. The relationship between Beijing and Moscow has become increasingly significant, particularly since 2022 when Putin sent troops into Ukraine. This move led to economic sanctions from the EU and the West, but China took advantage of the situation by increasing its purchases of Russian energy resources and becoming a key supplier of technologies, including high-tech components for Russia's military industries. Beijing is currently Moscow's top trading partner, with ties between the two nations strengthening over time. Meanwhile, Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, while Xi and Trump have held talks eight times, including a notable state visit to Washington by Xi in September. China's stance on the conflict in Ukraine has been met with skepticism by Western nations, who have urged Beijing to cut off supplies that could be used to fuel Russia's military actions. The Chinese government has maintained its neutrality in the conflict, while also accusing Kyiv's Western allies of playing a role in provoking Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This stance has been echoed by Moscow, which has repeatedly expressed support for China's position on issues related to Taiwan. Meanwhile, the recent diesel deal between the US and Russia has raised concerns about the potential consequences of such agreements, particularly given the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The trilateral meeting planned for APEC could potentially serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal, which has sparked worries among some leaders, including Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The global energy market has been affected by surging crude prices, with some attributing the rise to Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries. However, analysts argue that the Iran war is a more significant contributor to this trend. Some analysts have pointed out that the trilateral meeting could be an opportunity for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv's back, which has raised concerns among some leaders about being left out of negotiations. The unprecedented trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin on the sidelines of APEC has raised eyebrows among analysts who point out that any agreements reached in Shenzhen may not be enforceable on other parties. Peskov dismissed comparisons to the Yalta Conference, emphasizing that any potential deals struck in China would have no binding effect on others. articles.title: Nvidia at Center of Dispute Over Advanced Technology Exports to China
articles.summary: A public spat has erupted between two senior members of President Trump's administration over a high-stakes issue: controlling advanced technology exports to China.
articles.content: A public spat has erupted between two senior members of President Trump's administration over a high-stakes issue: controlling advanced technology exports to China. The controversy centers around Nvidia, a leading US-based chipmaker whose products are used in artificial intelligence and other cutting-edge technologies. At the heart of the dispute is an accusation made by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent against Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. According to Bessent, Lutnick failed to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia's most advanced chips, a move that could compromise national security and give Beijing a strategic advantage in emerging technologies. The issue has significant implications for the US-China trade relationship and reflects broader tensions between the two nations over technology transfer and intellectual property rights. With the stakes so high, it remains to be seen how this public disagreement will play out within the Trump administration and beyond. The relationship between the US government and China is complex, with different agencies having varying levels of influence over trade policies. Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, has expressed his affection for China, a sentiment that may have implications for the company's dealings in the country. Huang has been involved with Howard Lutnick, a key figure in the Trump administration, who shares his enthusiasm for China. According to reports, Lutnick wants Chinese companies to continue using American technology, including Nvidia's products. This stance is at odds with international concerns about the potential misuse of advanced chips by Beijing. Last year, the US Commerce Department and the Trump administration loosened restrictions on China buying less advanced Nvidia chips. However, this move may have inadvertently allowed companies collaborating with Beijing, such as Megaspeed, to gain access to more sophisticated technology. The export of high-end Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) has been a contentious issue in the US-China tech rivalry. According to Scott Bessent, frustration grew when President Trump made it explicitly clear that China should not receive advanced Nvidia chips beyond the H100 model. This stance was motivated by concerns about China's growing lead in artificial intelligence (AI). Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and former director of technology on President Biden's National Security Council staff, notes that if Chinese access to these chips were restricted, they would be significantly behind the US in AI development. The export restrictions have been continued into the Biden administration, with new regulations implemented in early 2025 requiring most foreign companies to obtain Commerce Department permission before purchasing advanced chips. The Commerce Department's decision to waive enforcement of its export restrictions on Nvidia chips has left foreign companies free to purchase them without permission. In May 2025, a new regulation was set to take effect, requiring most foreign companies to obtain approval from the Commerce Department before buying advanced chips from US-based companies like Nvidia. However, just two days before the regulation went into effect, the department announced that it would not be enforcing it, effectively allowing companies like Megaspeed to continue purchasing chips without restriction. As a result, Megaspeed was able to buy whatever it wanted without interruption. Megaspeed's ability to acquire Nvidia chips without interruption has significant implications for America's national security. The country's advantage in AI development could be lost if export controls are not properly implemented. The debate surrounding America's stance on exporting advanced technology to China will likely continue, with some arguing that it is a necessary step to maintain global competitiveness. Meanwhile, others believe that the risks associated with such exports outweigh any potential benefits. articles.title: Fiji Petrel Search Concludes with No Sightings
articles.summary: A team of scientists has concluded a 10-day search for one of the world's rarest birds, but unfortunately, the elusive Fiji petrel remained out of sight.
articles.content: A team of scientists has concluded a 10-day search for one of the world's rarest birds, but unfortunately, the elusive Fiji petrel remained out of sight. The expedition was conducted in partnership with National Geographic Pristine Seas and BirdLife International, with support from NatureFiji-MareqetiViti. The critically endangered bird is believed to have fewer than 50 individuals remaining on Earth, making it a top conservation priority. Community members on Gau Island, where the search took place, have pledged to protect the montane forests that are thought to be the bird's nesting grounds. Researchers managed to capture an audio recording of the Fiji petrel's call during their investigation, providing valuable insight into the bird's behavior and habitat. This unique sound is a significant contribution to the study of this enigmatic species. A paper detailing the expedition has been published in Bird Conservation International, offering a comprehensive review of historical sightings of the Fiji petrel and the findings of the 2025 at-sea survey and tagging attempt. The comprehensive review of historical sightings of the Fiji petrel includes every confirmed sighting from 1855 to the present day, providing a detailed picture of the species' presence over time. Despite being spotted on land on Gau until the 2000s, the last confirmed land sighting occurred in 2012, and since then there have been no further sightings. At sea, the last confirmed sighting was during a scientific search in 2023. This lack of nesting sites is a rare occurrence among seabird species. We're racing against time to save the Fiji petrel, said Lindsay Young, vice president of research for Pristine Seas, who led the expedition. The team employed tried-and-true techniques night and day, but unfortunately, the bird eluded them throughout their 10-day search. Meanwhile, local communities are taking steps to protect the bird's habitat. The scientists spent over 12 hours per day scouring the skies during their 10-day at-sea search, mostly in daylight hours. When the sun was out, they used a technique called chumming, releasing bait and fish oil on the sea surface to try and attract the birds. Spotlighting efforts at night aimed to draw in the petrels, using two handheld spotlights to create a strong beam visible from afar and an audio recording of calls meant to attract the bird on repeat. A mere 16 confirmed sightings of the Fiji petrel on land and 22 at sea have been documented by researchers. This scarcity of data has contributed significantly to the mystery surrounding this enigmatic species. The lack of understanding about the bird's habits is staggering, with its breeding patterns, population size, and foraging behavior remaining largely unknown. The team had hoped to shed some light on these secrets through a tagging effort, but after 10 days of intense searching, they came up empty-handed. A crucial component of their research involved consulting with residents of Gau Island, who possess traditional knowledge about the bird that has been passed down through generations. Through this collaboration, the team gained access to an invaluable resource: the only known audio recording of the Fiji petrel's call. The Fiji petrel holds a special place in Fijian culture and is featured on the country's 20-dollar banknote. Its significance extends beyond its cultural importance, with locals singing lullabies about the bird that have been passed down through generations on Gau Island, Fiji's fifth-largest island. Oral histories shared by village chiefs on Gau Island reveal a stark contrast to the bird's current scarcity. The island was once teeming with seabirds, including the Fiji petrel and similar species. Chiefs recalled stories from their great-grandmothers about collecting seabird eggs from the lower montane slopes behind the village. These egg collections were often made during pregnancy, when eating the eggs was considered desirable for a healthy outcome. Habitat degradation and invasive predators pose significant threats to the Fiji petrel's survival. Feral cats, rats, and pigs have ravaged the island's ecosystem, putting immense pressure on the remaining bird population. The recent expedition's lack of confirmed sightings has highlighted the perilous status of the Fiji petrel. External factors such as a cyclone that passed south of the area during the survey period and a strong El Niño event may also be contributing to the bird's absence. Scientists acknowledge that one survey is not enough to paint an accurate picture, but they cannot deny the real risk that the Fiji petrel may be slipping away. The Fiji petrel's elusive nature has left scientists scrambling to confirm its existence after a 10-day search yielded no conclusive evidence of the bird's presence. Despite the challenges, conservation efforts are underway to protect the bird's habitat and prevent further decline in its population. Communities are working together to safeguard the areas where the Fiji petrel is known to nest and feed, with hopes that their efforts will help stabilize the species' numbers. articles.content: A pop-up installation in the lobby of Hotel Prince de Galles in Paris has become a festive hotspot on Avenue George V, evoking the whimsical style of film director Wes Anderson. Each window inside the calendar reveals an imagined scenario, with some injecting humor and others evoking a sense of mystery, much like searching for Waldo in a crowded picture. Gohar likens these vignettes to the style of children's book author Richard Scarry, known for his detailed illustrations of cityscapes. Inside each window lies a chocolate treat from Casa Bosques, a design venture founded by Rafael Prieto, one of Gohar's friends and collaborators. These chocolates are infused with flavors that evoke the destinations featured in the advent calendar, adding an extra layer of sensory experience to the holiday tradition. Gohar's own background is marked by creative experimentation, having first gained recognition for her art pieces crafted from food materials before establishing her design studio, Gohar World. Advent calendars have become a staple in many cultures, evoking a sense of nostalgia and excitement among both children and adults alike. The anticipation of opening a new door or window each day can be quite thrilling, but it also requires a certain level of restraint, which can be challenging for kids to master. Gohar World's latest collection features exquisite pearl serving utensils that make for thoughtful gifts with a timeless quality. Hosting gatherings can be a significant undertaking, especially during holidays when expectations are high. By celebrating random everyday moments or events, she aims to alleviate pressure associated with traditional holiday gatherings. This approach encourages spontaneity and creativity in hosting. Laila's own experiences as a host have taught her that sometimes it's better to simplify and focus on what brings joy rather than striving for perfection. For instance, she once hosted a party centered around the beauty of dahlias discovered at the market, showcasing how everyday moments can become meaningful occasions. By merging fashion and design, she has created something special that inspires others to find beauty in everyday life. articles.summary: Several prominent women chefs have shared their travel plans for 2027, highlighting the exciting culinary adventures they're looking forward to embarking on next year.
articles.content: Traveling for inspiration has become a rare luxury for many professional chefs, given their demanding work schedules and responsibilities. However, taking time off to explore new culinary destinations is crucial for staying motivated and innovative in the kitchen. Even brief trips can have a lasting impact on one's cooking style, from discovering novel ingredients to mastering new techniques that elevate familiar dishes. These weekend getaways also offer opportunities to reconnect with one's heritage and network with fellow chefs who share similar passions. As 2027 approaches, several prominent women chefs have shared their travel plans with us, highlighting the exciting culinary adventures they're looking forward to embarking on next year. Several top chefs have expressed a desire to visit specific destinations in search of unique flavors and experiences that will enrich their cooking repertoire. Some are eager to explore lesser-known regions, such as the Basque Country in Spain, where foraged foods and traditional recipes await discovery. Edorta Lamo's restaurant in Kanpezu is one notable destination that has piqued their interest, offering a chance to experience authentic regional cuisine. The rugged beauty of the mountains is where some of the most authentic regional cuisine can be found. Inland cooking, built on what's locally hunted, foraged, and grown, offers a unique taste experience that can't be replicated elsewhere. Katie Button, chef and co-founder of Cúrate Bar de Tapas in Asheville, has her eyes set on exploring Maine next summer. She's particularly drawn to Erin French's new cookbook "Seize the Supper", which showcases local produce and a connection to the earth - principles that resonate deeply with Katie's own approach to regenerative cooking. For Camilla Marcus, chef and founder of Westbourne in Boulder, Colorado, it's all about experiencing the food culture of her friends Kelly Jeun and Eduardo Vallelobo at Casa Juani. Their restaurant recently made headlines as one of Bon Appétit's Best New Restaurants, and Camilla is eager to try their entirely Spanish menu. The culinary scene in Boulder has a lot to offer, but for Melissa Rodriguez, chef and partner at Crane Club & Bar CC in New York City, it's the opportunity to visit her friends Kelly Jeun and Eduardo Vallelobo that's the real draw. Edomae-style sushi is a rare find outside of Tokyo, but for those who know where to look, it's an experience not to be missed. Chef Mei Kougo's six-seat counter at [Sushi Meino] has been high on the list of many food enthusiasts since its opening in 2023 - although securing a reservation can be a challenge. The cuisine of Japan is renowned for its simplicity and focus on fresh ingredients, but it's not always easy to find restaurants that truly embody these principles. For those who are willing to seek out the best, however, the rewards are well worth the effort. For many, Tokyo remains a culinary paradise that beckons them back time and again. Rebekah Peppler, a recipe developer and author, is one such enthusiast who can't wait to return to Japan's vibrant food scene in the spring of 2027. Her travel plans are centered around experiencing the renowned temple food in Jangseong County, South Korea. However, she was disappointed when she missed out on the opportunity to dine at Jeong Kwan and Chef Esu Lee's collaborative culinary event at Orson in Paris recently. Lebanese cuisine is another destination that beckons her heart, particularly its distinctive street foods like manakish and shawarma. As someone with Lebanese heritage, Chef Mary Attea is familiar with the country's rich culinary traditions. However, growing up in the US, she often only experienced a small fraction of Lebanon's gastronomic diversity. Now, she longs to immerse herself in the full spectrum of Lebanese cuisine and explore its beauty firsthand. Peruvian cuisine has long fascinated chefs around the world, particularly when it comes to its take on ceviche. To truly experience the essence of Peruvian cuisine, Norma Listman, chef and co-founder of Masala y Maíz in Mexico City, wants to immerse herself in its culinary traditions while exploring the country's broader cultural landscape. This involves delving into the shared histories and connections between Latin American cultures that are often overlooked. Peru is home to a rich tapestry of traditional markets where local ingredients, people, and customs come together around food. articles.title: Hair Loss Linked to Aging Due to Smaller Hair Follicles
articles.summary: Hair loss after 50 is a common phenomenon, but it's not an inevitable part of aging. Many women experience changes in their hair as they approach this milestone age. According to...
articles.content: Hair loss after 50 is a common phenomenon, but it's not an inevitable part of aging. Many women experience changes in their hair as they approach this milestone age. According to trichologist Sharley Viola, these changes are linked to shifts in the hair growth cycle. As we age, our hair follicles gradually become smaller, leading to finer, shorter strands that lose pigment. This process is known as follicular miniaturization. The impact of aging on hair can be attributed to a combination of factors, including thyroid function and circulation. Biochemist Jared Reynolds notes that these underlying health issues can contribute to hair thinning. Hair care experts stress that it's essential to understand the root cause of hair loss before addressing it. A thorough examination of one's overall health can provide valuable insights into potential triggers for hair thinning. Declining thyroid activity with age can have a significant impact on hair growth and overall health. This decline can lead to thyroid imbalances that affect not just hair texture but also follicle health. In some cases, medications used to manage these imbalances can further exacerbate the issue. Reduced blood circulation within the scalp's microcirculatory system is another factor contributing to hair thinning in older individuals. As we age, this system becomes less efficient at supplying oxygen and nutrients to the hair follicles, which are essential for healthy growth. This reduction in circulation can be particularly problematic if left unaddressed. Hair loss prevention strategies often hinge on identifying its underlying causes, with some types being more preventable than others. For instance, hair thinning caused by age-related hormonal and follicular changes may not always be avoidable, but other factors such as thyroid imbalances or certain medications can be managed through medical treatment under a healthcare professional's guidance. Understanding the underlying causes of hair thinning after 50 is crucial in determining the most effective treatment approach. Medical professionals can help identify the root cause of hair loss and recommend personalized solutions. Topical treatments such as minoxidil have been shown to promote hair regrowth, according to Viola. However, styling products can also play a significant role in making thinning hair appear more voluminous. Sabina Wizemann, Director at the GH Beauty Personal Care Lab, advises against using heavy hair products that weigh down the hair. Instead, she recommends using volumizing mousses and root-lifting sprays to create lift and body throughout the lengths of fine and thinning hair. These styling options can help add volume without leaving the hair looking limp. For those who have tried topical treatments to no avail, there are in-office options available to stimulate hair growth. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) therapy involves scalp injections that can stimulate growth, while low-level laser therapy uses low-intensity light to encourage new hair development. A dermatologist should be consulted for these procedures. Reynolds emphasizes the importance of patience and consistency when trying to achieve desired results. It may take time to see noticeable improvements, but with a consistent routine, it is possible to achieve hair that boosts confidence. articles.title: Breakthrough in Bioprinting Technology Using Modified 3D Printer
articles.summary: A breakthrough in bioprinting technology has been announced by researchers at the University of Rochester, who have successfully modified a standard $450 3D printer to create living...
articles.content: A breakthrough in bioprinting technology has been announced by researchers at the University of Rochester, who have successfully modified a standard $450 3D printer to create living materials with over 100 layers. The team, led by Professor Anne S. Meyer, aimed to make DIY bioprinters affordable and accessible to scientists worldwide by using inexpensive parts that are easily obtainable. According to Meyer, the goal is to enable other researchers to create these bioprinters in their own labs without breaking the bank. The modified 3D printer replaces the plastic filament extruder with a syringe pump that dispenses bio-ink, a specialized formula combining living cells and a polymer solution. This unique mixture hardens into a gel once printed, setting it apart from traditional bioprinted materials. Using this low-cost setup, researchers can create living tissues with precise control over cell types and final shape. The possibilities are vast, ranging from cleaning up contaminated water to breaking down waste materials like plastic. The team's innovative approach addresses the significant drawback of current 3D bioprinters: their high cost and tendency to collapse before setting. The customized bioprinter's syringe is capable of both extrusion and retraction, preventing unwanted oozing at the edges of printed structures. This innovative setup allows for the creation of crisp shapes with well-defined edges, a significant improvement over previous DIY 3D bioprinters. The cost of this upgraded printer was remarkably low, thanks to its components being easily sourced from various suppliers. As a result, other labs can now build their own version of the printer and syringe pump. The new DIY bioprinter has expanded the possibilities for printing living structures by allowing for more than 100 layers. In contrast, previous versions were limited to fewer than 20 layers. This significant increase in complexity and height enables researchers to create hollow cavities within printed structures. The upgraded printer's capabilities open up new avenues for creating structures with a high surface-to-volume ratio. This allows embedded bacteria to efficiently receive signals or nutrients from their surroundings and excrete useful products at an accelerated rate. To facilitate the printing process, researchers developed a support gel called slurry that holds up bio-ink and helps it solidify quickly at any height. Two types of slurry were created: one for easy removal of the print and another designed for incubation that allows microbes in the bioprints to remain alive for four or more weeks. The versatility of this new slurry is vast, enabling researchers to create engineered biofilm materials that can mimic the characteristics of real-world biofilms or possess enhanced mechanical properties. Researchers can now test and study these artificially created biofilms in a controlled environment, gaining valuable insights into their behavior and interactions with surfaces. This breakthrough has significant implications for various fields, including medicine, where understanding biofilms is crucial for developing effective treatments. The creation of living materials with more than 100 layers using this modified $450 3D printer marks a major advancement in bioprinting technology, opening up new avenues for research and development in fields that rely on complex structures. articles.title: Walking After Meals Reduces Blood Sugar Levels
articles.summary: A recent study suggests that walking post-meal can boost metabolism and regulate blood sugar levels.
articles.content: A recent change in my evening routine has left me feeling more energized than ever, and it's all thanks to a simple yet effective habit - walking after every meal. Every night, as colleagues finish their dinner at a restaurant in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, I slip out of the door for a brisk 10-minute walk home. This daily ritual began months ago when I stumbled upon a TikTok video from a nutritionist who claimed that short walks post-meal could boost metabolism and regulate blood sugar levels. The concept resonated with me, especially since I'm an avid walker and eater - two pastimes that are not mutually exclusive, as it turns out. According to internal medicine physician Elizabeth Sharp Edens, prolonged sitting after meals can lead to a higher post-meal blood-sugar response, but breaking it up with short walks can make a significant difference. Physician Elizabeth Sharp Edens explains that while brief periods of sitting after eating aren't inherently bad, prolonged inactivity can have negative consequences. My friend Elizabeth Sharp Edens, an internal medicine and obesity medicine physician, has shed some light on the topic. Research has shown that incorporating light-intensity walking into daily routines can have a significant impact on post-meal glucose levels. According to a 2022 meta-analysis published in Sports Medicine, walking after meals reduced glucose by nearly 17 percent. The science behind this phenomenon lies in the way muscles use glucose for energy when we walk. As Edens points out, our legs contain some of the largest muscles in the body, which makes sense given that walking stimulates muscle contractions that facilitate the movement of glucose transporters. This natural process can be a game-changer for those who struggle with feeling overly full or experiencing afternoon energy crashes. Rather than relying on supplements or peptides, walking offers an easy and free solution to improve digestion and prevent blood-sugar dips. Walking after meals can alleviate feelings of discomfort and fullness. According to research, a slow walk after a meal accelerates stomach emptying by reducing the time it takes for half its contents to be digested. This is particularly beneficial for individuals experiencing bloating, as mild walking has been shown to decrease intestinal gas retention from 45 percent to 24 percent and alleviate symptoms. Gravity also plays a role in digestion, notes Caitlin Hosmer, a registered dietitian based in Maine. She explains that walking can help mitigate uncomfortable fullness and reflux after meals due to the effects of gravity on digestion. Studies have demonstrated that even brief periods of walking can be effective in reducing post-meal glucose spikes. A 2025 study found that a 10-minute walk lowered glucose measurements by 6 percent, while a 30-minute walk resulted in a 5 percent decrease in glucose levels. Getting started on post-meal walks requires minimal effort and commitment. If you can manage just a short 10-minute stroll, it's better than nothing. In fact, even this brief period of movement has been shown to have a positive impact on glucose levels. The science behind why walking after meals is beneficial lies in the timing. According to Hosmer, glucose typically peaks within an hour or so after eating. By moving before this peak, individuals can effectively blunt the spike in glucose levels that often follows a meal. This simple yet effective strategy has been observed to yield significant results. Incorporating post-meal walks into daily routines may seem like a challenge, especially when time is of the essence. By incorporating post-meal walks into daily routines, individuals can experience a significant reduction in lethargy after eating.
